items.stem: During a three-week period, an employer-caused design delay and a contractor-caused labour shortage both independently delay completion. Under a typical analysis, what does true concurrent delay usually mean for entitlement?

options.text: The contractor is generally entitled to time but not necessarily to prolongation cost
options.rationale: Correct: concurrency commonly grants an extension of time while barring prolongation cost for the overlap.

options.text: The contractor is entitled to both time and full prolongation cost
options.rationale: Its own concurrent culpable delay usually bars recovery of cost for the overlapping period.

options.text: The contractor loses all entitlement to time
options.rationale: The excusable employer delay still supports time entitlement.

options.text: Liquidated damages automatically apply for the whole period
options.rationale: The excusable delay means LADs do not simply run through the concurrent period.

items.explanation: Correct: concurrency commonly grants an extension of time while barring prolongation cost for the overlap.

items.stem: Which TWO conditions make an as-planned-versus-as-built delay analysis a suitable choice? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reliable as-built progress records exist for the delayed work
options.rationale: Correct: the method compares planned to actual, so trustworthy as-built data is essential.

options.text: A logic-linked baseline programme is available
options.rationale: Correct: a sound baseline gives the planned intent to compare against.

options.text: No progress records were kept during the works
options.rationale: Without as-built data the comparison cannot be made.

options.text: The analysis must be done before the works start
options.rationale: As-planned-vs-as-built is retrospective; it needs completed-work data.

items.explanation: Correct: the method compares planned to actual, so trustworthy as-built data is essential.

items.stem: A claim states only that 'the employer caused 40 days of delay overall' without linking events to effects. What is the main weakness?

options.text: It is a global claim that fails to show cause and effect for each event
options.rationale: Correct: tribunals expect each delay event particularised with its effect on completion.

options.text: It claims too few days to be worth pursuing
options.rationale: The quantum is not the issue; the lack of particularisation is.

options.text: Global claims are always accepted without evidence
options.rationale: Global claims are generally disfavoured and vulnerable to challenge.
Employer delays can found entitlement; they must be properly evidenced.

items.explanation: Correct: tribunals expect each delay event particularised with its effect on completion.
